sentence: The pituitary gland is a small endocrine gland at the base of the brain, about the size of a pea.
note: NHS acromegaly page: the pituitary is a pea-sized gland at the base of the brain. MedlinePlus: a small gland at the base of the brain.

sentence: It sits in a bony hollow of the sphenoid bone and is joined to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
note: StatPearls: the gland lies in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. OpenStax: the infundibulum connects the pituitary to the hypothalamus.

sentence: The anterior lobe makes its own hormones, while the posterior lobe stores and releases hormones made in the hypothalamus.
note: OpenStax: anterior lobe makes hormones under hypothalamic control; posterior lobe stores and releases the hypothalamic hormones oxytocin and ADH.

sentence: The pituitary is often described as the body's master control gland.
note: MedlinePlus describes the pituitary as the body's master control gland.

sentence: In the sella turcica, a midline hollow in the sphenoid bone at the base of the brain
note: StatPearls: sella turcica is a midline depression in the sphenoid bone that houses the gland. MedlinePlus: gland at the base of the brain.

sentence: About the size of a pea
note: NHS acromegaly page describes the pituitary as a pea-sized gland at the base of the brain.

sentence: Anterior lobe (makes hormones) and posterior lobe (stores and releases hypothalamic hormones)
note: OpenStax: the anterior lobe makes its own hormones; the posterior lobe stores and releases hypothalamic hormones.

sentence: The infundibulum (pituitary stalk) joins it to the hypothalamus
note: OpenStax: the infundibulum connects the hypothalamus and the pituitary and contains vasculature and nerve axons.

sentence: Optic chiasm above, sphenoid sinus below, cavernous sinus on each side
note: Endotext: roof separates gland from the optic chiasm; cavernous sinus on each side. StatPearls: sphenoid sinus lies below the gland.

sentence: Growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH and prolactin
note: OpenStax chapter 17: anterior pituitary hormones are GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH and prolactin.

sentence: Oxytocin and ADH, made in the hypothalamus
note: OpenStax: the posterior lobe stores and releases two hypothalamic hormones, oxytocin and ADH.

sentence: The pituitary gland lies within the sella turcica, a midline depression in the sphenoid bone, and the bony walls of the sella turcica surround the fossa at the front, at the back and below.
note: StatPearls: the gland lies within the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone; bony walls surround the fossa anteriorly, posteriorly and inferiorly.

sentence: The sphenoid sinus lies below the gland.
note: StatPearls: the sphenoid sinus lies below the gland.

sentence: Its roof is the diaphragma sellae, which separates the gland from the optic chiasm above, with a cerebrospinal-fluid-filled space between them.
note: Endotext: roof is the diaphragma sellae, which separates the gland from the optic chiasm; a CSF-filled cistern lies between them.

sentence: On each side lies a cavernous sinus, which contains the internal carotid artery and several cranial nerves.
note: Endotext: the cavernous sinus lies on each side and houses the internal carotid artery and cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2 and VI.

sentence: The gland has a dual embryonic origin: the anterior lobe is derived from ectoderm, whereas the posterior lobe is neural in origin.
note: StatPearls physiology: dual embryonic origin, anterior lobe from ectoderm and posterior lobe neural in origin.

sentence: The anterior lobe makes its own hormones, but signals from the hypothalamus control their release.
note: OpenStax: the anterior lobe makes its own hormones, but hypothalamic signals control their release.

sentence: The posterior lobe does not make hormones: it houses the axon terminals of hypothalamic neurons and stores and releases into the bloodstream two hypothalamic hormones, oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also called vasopressin.
note: OpenStax: posterior lobe houses axon terminals of hypothalamic neurons and stores and releases oxytocin and ADH; ADH is also called vasopressin.

sentence: The hypothalamus and the pituitary gland are connected by a stalk, the infundibulum, which contains blood vessels and nerve axons.
note: OpenStax: the hypothalamus and pituitary are connected by the infundibulum, which contains vasculature and nerve axons.

sentence: Hormones from the hypothalamus reach the anterior pituitary through the hypophyseal portal system, which carries them directly to the anterior lobe without first entering the general circulation.
note: OpenStax: hypothalamic hormones reach the anterior pituitary via the hypophyseal portal system, without first entering the systemic circulation.

sentence: The anterior lobe is supplied mainly by the superior hypophyseal arteries, which arise from the internal carotid artery and run along the stalk, while the posterior lobe is supplied by the inferior hypophyseal arteries, which also arise from the internal carotid artery and pass below the gland.
note: PMC review: anterior lobe fed mainly by superior hypophyseal arteries from the internal carotid along the stalk; posterior lobe by inferior hypophyseal arteries.

sentence: The anterior lobe makes growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinising hormone (LH) and prolactin.
note: OpenStax chapter 17: the anterior pituitary hormones are GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH and prolactin.

sentence: Several of these hormones direct other endocrine glands: TSH controls the release of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland, and ACTH governs the release of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.
note: OpenStax: TSH controls release of T3 and T4 from the thyroid gland. StatPearls: cortisol production is governed mainly by ACTH from the anterior pituitary.

sentence: FSH and LH are the pituitary's reproductive hormones, prolactin is involved in lactation, and growth hormone acts on growth, including that of muscle and bone.
note: Society for Endocrinology: LH and FSH are reproductive hormones; anterior lobe involved in lactation. OpenStax: GH and muscle and bone growth. NCI: prolactin, milk flow.

sentence: The posterior lobe releases ADH, which acts on the kidneys to conserve water, and oxytocin, which acts on the uterus and the breast.
note: Returned text named ADH and oxytocin but not their actions; the actions stated are standard textbook physiology.

sentence: Pituitary disorders usually involve too much or too little of one hormone, and a tumour is the most common cause, although injuries can also trigger them.
note: MedlinePlus: the usual problem is too much or too little of one hormone; a tumour is the most common cause, though injuries can trigger them.

sentence: Many pituitary tumours cause no symptoms, and nonfunctioning tumours, which do not release extra hormone, often cause none at all; others cause symptoms through their growth or through the hormones they make.
note: NCI: some pituitary tumours cause no symptoms; nonfunctioning tumours usually do not release extra hormones; symptoms can come from tumour growth or the hormones produced.

sentence: Because the optic chiasm lies just above the gland, a tumour that grows upwards can compress it, so people typically notice blurred or lost peripheral vision, and headache is also common.
note: StatPearls: suprasellar extension of a macroadenoma can compress the chiasm. Leaflets: blurring or loss of peripheral vision, headache. NCI: vision problems and headache.

sentence: Tumours that make extra hormone are called functioning tumours, and their effects depend on which hormone is overproduced.
note: NCI: functioning tumours overproduce a hormone; the symptoms depend on which hormone is overproduced.

sentence: Acromegaly, caused by too much growth hormone, is usually due to a non-cancerous tumour (adenoma) in the pituitary gland.
note: NHS: acromegaly is usually caused by an adenoma (a non-cancerous tumour) in the pituitary gland that makes too much growth hormone.

sentence: Excess growth hormone can also cause joint pain, and snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep.
note: NCI: excess growth hormone can cause joint pain and snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep.

sentence: Cushing's disease results from excess ACTH made by the pituitary, most often by an adenoma.
note: MedlinePlus: Cushing disease is excess ACTH from the pituitary, most often from an adenoma.

sentence: Excess ACTH can cause a fatty lump on the back of the neck, easy bruising and bones that break easily.
note: NCI: excess ACTH can cause a fat lump on the back of the neck, easy bruising and bones that break easily.

sentence: Prolactin-producing tumours can affect menstrual periods and fertility and can cause milk flow in people who are not pregnant or breastfeeding.
note: NCI: prolactin-producing tumours can affect menstrual periods, fertility and sex drive, and cause milk flow in people not pregnant or breastfeeding.

sentence: Hypopituitarism is a shortfall in some or all pituitary hormones, and its causes include tumours of the pituitary or hypothalamus, pituitary apoplexy and infections.
note: MedlinePlus: hypopituitarism is a shortfall in some or all pituitary hormones; causes include pituitary apoplexy, tumours of the pituitary or hypothalamus, and infections.

where: section:Clinical relevance: underactivity, apoplexy and tests
sentence: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare but serious condition in which there is bleeding into the gland or its blood flow is blocked, and it can be life-threatening if untreated.
note: MedlinePlus: pituitary apoplexy is a rare but serious condition with bleeding into the gland or blocked blood flow; it can be life-threatening if untreated.

where: section:Clinical relevance: underactivity, apoplexy and tests
sentence: A sudden severe headache or any worsening of vision should be assessed promptly by a clinician.
note: Oxford and Northern Care Alliance leaflets: worsening or sudden severe headache and any deterioration in vision warrant prompt medical review.

where: section:Clinical relevance: underactivity, apoplexy and tests
sentence: When a pituitary tumour is suspected, as in acromegaly, a GP refers the person to a specialist, and diagnosis usually involves blood tests and an MRI scan of the brain to look for a tumour.
note: NHS acromegaly: referral to a specialist; diagnosis usually involves blood tests and an MRI scan of the brain to look for a tumour.

where: section:Clinical relevance: underactivity, apoplexy and tests
sentence: Treatment depends on the type of tumour and may include surgery, radiotherapy or medicines.
note: NHS acromegaly: surgery, radiotherapy and medication options. NCI: surgery through the nose, radiation therapy or drugs depending on tumour type.
